title: Flat Noetherian pointed model retaining the distinguished reduced fibre and section components
statement: Let $g:P\to T$ be a flat morphism [def-weil-flat-morphism] of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]), with a section $\sigma:T\to P$, $g\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_T$, and a point $q\in P$. Schemes and sections are as in [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-section]. Assume the fibre $P_{g(q)}$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. For any morphism $h:Y\to B$ with section $e$, write $C(h,e)=\{y\in Y\mid y\text{ belongs to the connected component of }e(h(y))\text{ in }h^{-1}(\{h(y)\})\}$ [def-weil-connected-scheme]. There exist an affine open $V\subseteq T$ containing $g(q)$, Noetherian schemes $P_0,T_0$ (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact), with $T_0$ affine, a flat morphism $g_0:P_0\to T_0$ of finite presentation, a section $\sigma_0:T_0\to P_0$, and maps $b:V\to T_0$, $\rho:P_V\to P_0$, where $P_V=P\times_TV$ [def-pc-base-change]. Writing $g_V:P_V\to V$ and $\sigma_V:V\to P_V$ for the induced morphism and section, the square $(\rho,g_V;g_0,b)$ is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product], $g_0\circ\sigma_0=\mathrm{id}_{T_0}$, and $\rho\circ\sigma_V=\sigma_0\circ b$. Put $q_0=\rho(q)$ and $t_0=g_0(q_0)$, identifying $P_V$ with $g^{-1}(V)$. The geometric fibre $(P_0)_{\bar t_0}$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and $\rho^{-1}C(g_0,\sigma_0)=C(g,\sigma)\cap P_V$. No condition is asserted on the other fibres of $g_0$.

source.place: Tag 055Q, lemma-connected-along-section-open-neighbourhood, first paragraph: affine restriction, descent of family and section, eventual flatness, and the distinguished fibre

proof.text: Put $t=g(q)$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ containing $t$, using the affine-open basis. The restriction $P_V=P\times_TV\to V$ is flat by flat base change and is of finite presentation by finite-presentation base change. Define $\sigma_V=(\sigma|_V,\mathrm{id}_V)$ by the fibre-product universal property; its second projection is the identity, so it is a section. The open base change identifies $P_V$ with $g^{-1}(V)$ and retains $q$.

source.place: Tag 055Q, first sentence; Tags 01IT (affine-open basis), 01U9 (flat base change), 01TS (finite-presentation base change)

proof.text: Index the finitely generated integer subalgebras $A_i\subseteq A$ by inclusion. They form a set (each is a subset of $A$), are nonempty (the image of $\mathbf Z$ is one), and are directed: adjoining the union of two finite generating sets gives a common upper bound. Put $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. The affine approximation lemma gives $V=\varprojlim_iT_i$ with affine transitions and every $T_i$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$. Each $T_i$ is Noetherian by the finite-type Noetherian theorem. The affine-base qcqs lemma, applied to the identity of $T_i$, gives that $T_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus this directed system satisfies the hypotheses of finite-presentation descent.

source.place: Tag 055Q, first paragraph: write A as a directed colimit of finite-type integer algebras; Tag 01T6

proof.text: Apply finite-presentation descent (Tag 01ZM(1), Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation) to the affine Noetherian approximation N of V. This gives a stage i, a finitely presented p:Y→N_i and a cartesian square recovering P_V→V. All stages are Noetherian and qcqs; since p is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, Y is qcqs. The underlying index of N is the directed partial order of finitely generated integer subalgebras, with the arrows reversed.

source.place: Tag 055Q, first paragraph: descend the family; Tag 01ZM(1), lemma-descend-finite-presentation

proof.text: Advance first to a flat stage, before descending the section. Regard p:Y→N_i as the morphism Over.mk p→Over.mk(id_N_i). Its pullback over V is flat: composition with the isomorphism N_i×_{N_i}V→V identifies it with P_V→V through the cartesian comparison isomorphism. Apply exists_flat_stage_of_limit to this morphism. At the returned larger subalgebra j, composition with the analogous identity-pullback isomorphism gives Flat(p_j). Pullback pasting and cancellation give a cartesian comparison P_V→Y_j over V→N_j. Finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness persist by base change.

source.place: Tag 055Q first paragraph; eventual flatness is Tag 04AI. The independent descent of the section can be performed after this stage increase.

proof.text: Restrict the affine approximation to Over j; this forgetful functor is initial, so its whiskered cone still has limit V. Compose the given section with P_V→Y_j. This is a map over N_j, since the original section identity and the cartesian square imply the required composite equality. Apply the over-base morphism clause of Tag 01ZM, in its source-equal-to-the-base form Scheme.exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation. Obtain a later stage k and τ:N_k→Y_j with τ≫p_j=N(k→j) and b_k≫τ equal to the composite of the original section with P_V→Y_j. Set P₀=Y_j×_{N_j}N_k, T₀=N_k, g₀=pr₂, and σ₀=(τ,id). Then σ₀≫g₀=id by the second projection. Lift the comparison to ρ:P_V→P₀ using its maps to Y_j and N_k. Pullback cancellation proves that (ρ,g_V;g₀,b_k) is cartesian. Checking its two projections proves σ_V≫ρ=b_k≫σ₀. Flatness and finite presentation persist by base change. Mathlib gives LocallyOfFiniteType directly from LocallyOfFinitePresentation (finite-presentation ring maps are finite type). Thus the finite-type Noetherian theorem and quasi-compactness give IsNoetherian P₀. The stage T₀ is affine and Noetherian. These constructions work for empty sources and do not assume the section component contains q.

source.place: Tag 055Q first paragraph; Tag 01ZM morphism descent, Tag 01T6 for the Noetherian source.

proof.text: Put v=⟨g(q),hq⟩ in V and t₀=b(v). The residue-field fibre square induced by the restriction P_V→P shows by base-change stability that the fibre of g_V at v is geometrically reduced, using the assumed geometrically reduced fibre of g at g(q). For every algebraic closure Ω of κ(v), pullback pasting identifies the geometric fibre with the scalar extension of this scheme-theoretic fibre, hence it is reduced. The model square supplies the comparison isomorphism P_V≅P₀×_{T₀}V over V. Its base change along Spec Ω→V is an isomorphism of geometric fibres, so the canonical pullback family P₀×_{T₀}V also has reduced geometric fibre at v. Apply geometricReduced_fibre_locus_baseChange to (g₀,b). Membership in its left-hand locus at v implies membership in the right-hand inverse-image locus, hence reducedness for every algebraic closure over b(v). Specialize to AlgebraicClosure(κ(b(v))). No assertion on other fibres or surjectivity of b is used.

source.place: Tag 055Q, first paragraph: X_y is the base change of X_{i,y_i}; Tag 0576, lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced, using Tag 0384, lemma-geometrically-reduced-upstairs

proof.text: Both g₀ and g are locally of finite type by the Mathlib instance from local finite presentation. Apply section_component_preimage_of_isPullback to the model square (ρ,g_V;g₀,b) with its compatible sections. This identifies ρ⁻¹C(g₀,σ₀) with C(g_V,σ_V). Apply the same lemma to the canonical restriction square (pr₁,g_V;g,V.ι); sectionBaseChange has the required section identity and first projection. This identifies pr₁⁻¹C(g,σ) with the same locus C(g_V,σ_V). Rewriting both equalities gives the required displayed equality, completing all clauses.
